restatement: The card replaces the two copies of FOR iteration (plain FOR and TABLE-FOR) with one loop runner on a chained scope stack. A frame holds the item name and the @ metadata and has a parent link. FOR gains limit= and offset= (a literal or a path read outside the loop, validated as a non-negative safe integer in every mode, with missing data governed by strict mode), an {{ELSE}} empty branch rendered in the outer scope, and @total. Conditions, math, filters, ternary, CASE and LIST_ITEM must read through the scope chain without copying the caller's data map. Non-root path segments read own properties only. Iterations, stats and output stay bounded. analyze, render and spec must agree. No runtime dependency, no eval, and no change to previously valid output beyond the two approved exceptions (trailing words after the item name, inherited segments).
brief_mismatch: Four inconsistencies in the brief. (1) Must-not m1 and criterion c10 forbid changing any existing test file or expectation, with no carve-out. card.md's must-not allows 'the one named amendment (if any)', and spec.md Notes say 56 rows of the card's own test file were corrected under card.json test_amendments. The packet does not show those amendments or who approved them, and the scope-exceptions log covers only spec.md. (2) The manifest lists tests/language/for-window.test.ts as an add, but the diff shows it as an edit of a file that existed at base (index fbc5b52..8bd5691). The lead's post-freeze amendment corrected this only for the four golden-case files. (3) c9 in the criteria and card.md names `@parent.constructor`, but spec.md's fw-own drops it and lists @parent as a non-goal, so that part of c9 cannot be tested on this card. (4) The packet marks the TABLE non-ROW rule as a polish question, but spec.md Notes ask the reviewer to confirm that no previously valid template changes meaning. That is m5, a must-not, so I file the hit as goal-risk and not drift.
verification_plan: c1: confirm that the parser accepts limit/offset as a decimal literal or a variable path, and that the runtime check rejects negative, fractional, non-numeric, boolean, array, object, NaN, Infinity and unsafe values with a type-error relocated to the FOR in both modes, including a non-iterable in lenient mode or under the TABLE legacy rule; a missing/null/undefined path is missing-variable naming the full path in strict mode and is ignored in lenient mode; the window paths are read before the loop frame is pushed.
c2: confirm @index0..@notLast are computed over the windowed slice, @total equals the slice length on every iteration, and @total is absent from the root scope.

c3: confirm the ELSE body renders only when the slice is empty, renders in the outer scope with no item or @ names bound, a strict non-iterable still throws the located type-error before the ELSE, the parser takes ELSE only when it is directly in the FOR body, a second ELSE is a syntax-error at that tag, and IF/ELSEIF/SECTION handling of ELSE is unchanged.

c4: confirm the FOR header tokenizer rejects unknown keys, repeats, upper-case keys, quoted or empty values, spaces around =, commas, trailing words and a missing item name, all at the FOR token, at parse time (so also in branches that never render, and in validate and analyze).
c5: confirm TABLE-FOR calls the same runner with a silent non-iterable flag, ELSE ROWs render for a non-iterable, the window and @total apply, and the non-ROW fallback keeps its old meaning.
c6: confirm countIteration runs once per rendered item and never for skipped items, and the output check runs after each item and after the ELSE body (TABLE rows included).
c7: confirm the frame is pushed and popped with try/finally, frames carry a parent, inner shadowing is local, and interpret() resets to the root.

c8: confirm getAllVariables is gone and every evaluateCondition/evaluateMathExpression call receives the scope chain, and that the root wraps the map without calling iterator, entries, keys or forEach, also on error paths.
c9: confirm one own-property helper is used by the interpreter and by expressions for non-root object segments, and how arrays and strings handle inherited names.
c10/m1: check that no pre-existing test file changed and that the frozen card tests did not change.
m2/m3: no new imports from packages; no template-built RegExp or eval.
m5: look for previously valid templates whose output changes beyond the two approved exceptions (FOR header parsing, TABLE fallback grouping, scope lookup).
analyze/spec: window path roots recorded as usage 'for' before the loop name is scoped, ELSE body walked once without the loop name, spec FOR/ELSE text updated.

findings.title: The frozen card test file was edited to weaken 56 strict-mode expectations

serves.scenario: tests/language/for-window.test.ts existed at base and is presented as frozen. The diff turns its strict-mode missing-variable expectations into plain output for inherited segments (output, condition, loop item, math with x.constructor + 1 now expecting empty) and for @total in an IF condition outside a loop. A builder who changes the frozen test to fit the code removes the check the plan relied on, against m1 ('change any existing test expectation or existing test file') and c10 ('no existing test file changes'). The new expectations agree with language-contract.md ('a condition never raises a missing-variable error') and with the old silent behaviour for missing non-root segments. Whether the change is legitimate therefore depends on an approval this packet does not show.

findings.rubric: m1, c10; frozen-tests rule of the packet (a change to a frozen test is a deviation from the plan)
findings.reproduction: Compare base and head of tests/language/for-window.test.ts. The fw-meta row '@total in an IF condition outside a loop' changes from SL(ERR('missing-variable',1,1), OUT('N')) to OUT('N'). The fw-own rows for constructor, __proto__, toString, hasOwnProperty and valueOf change from SL(ERR(...), OUT(...)) to OUT(...), and the math row changes from strict ERR to OUT(''). The rows for xs.constructor and s.toString change the same way. The scope-exceptions log has no row for this file. The smallest restoring change: get the lead's recorded approval of exactly these 56 rows in card.json test_amendments, or revert the edits and make strict mode raise missing-variable for those reads.
evidence: test:fw-meta: [render-strict] @total in an IF condition outside a loop

findings.title: The TABLE-FOR fallback now merges separate non-ROW body nodes into one row, changing previously valid tables

serves.scenario: Before, each non-ROW node in a TABLE FOR body was rendered and split on '|' alone, so a body of two IF blocks that each render one row gave two rows per item. tableRowsFrom now joins every consecutive non-ROW node into one string and splits it on '|' once. The same template gives one row per item, its cells join text across the line break (for example '1', a newline, then 'B'), and the markdown table breaks. m5 allows only two output changes (trailing FOR words and inherited segments), and this is neither.

findings.rubric: m5; spec Notes ('A reviewer should confirm no previously valid template changes meaning'); polish question on TABLE legacy rules
findings.reproduction: resolveTemplate on '{{TABLE}}{{HEADER}}K|V{{END_HEADER}}{{FOR xs AS x}}' + newline + '{{IF x.a}}A|1{{END_IF}}' + newline + '{{IF x.b}}B|2{{END_IF}}' + newline + '{{END_FOR}}{{END_TABLE}}' with xs = [{a:true,b:true}]. At base the output has rows '| A | 1 |' and '| B | 2 |'. At head it has one row whose middle cell holds '1', a line break and 'B'. The smallest restoring change: split the merged run into lines before splitting each non-blank line on '|'. That keeps the frozen case '${{x}}|${{@index0}}' as one row and keeps one row per line.

findings.title: A FOR iterable that contains whitespace, which rendered before, is now a syntax error

serves.scenario: The old header regex /FOR\s+(.+?)\s+AS\s+(\w+)/i took everything up to the first ' AS ' as the iterable, so '{{FOR my items AS x}}' read the data key 'my items'. Data keys with spaces are plausible: the language contract treats names such as 'Order #' as plain data. parseForHeader now requires words[2] to be AS, so the same template is 'Invalid FOR syntax'. The words involved come before the item name, so this is not the approved 'trailing words after the FOR item name' exception.

findings.reproduction: resolveTemplate('{{FOR my items AS x}}${{x}}{{END_FOR}}', new Map([['my items', ['a']]])) returns 'a' at base. At head it throws syntax-error 'Invalid FOR syntax'. The smallest restoring change: find the first standalone AS word (case-insensitive) after FOR and take words[1..asIndex-1] joined by a space as the iterable, then parse the item name and arguments after it.

findings.title: The error path still lists every data key, and does it through Map.prototype.keys, which the fw-no-copy test does not count

serves.scenario: RootScope.names() calls Map.prototype.keys.call(this.data) and Array.from on the result, so a strict missing-variable error still lists every key of the data map. It does this on purpose through the built-in method, which bypasses the CountingMap overrides. The test 'a loop that errors out still makes no copy' therefore passes without observing the enumeration it was written to forbid. The cost is one read on an error, not one per condition, so the c8 goal (no copy per condition) still holds, but the test no longer proves what its name says.

findings.rubric: c8; reviewer question on copies of the data map
findings.reproduction: Run the fw-no-copy error-path case with a Map subclass that counts calls to Map.prototype.keys (or wrap the MapIterator). The data map's key list is enumerated once when MissingVariableError is built. Note for the lead: either accept the one-time read on errors and record it in the spec, or document that the suggestion list bypasses overrides.
evidence: test:fw-no-copy: a loop that errors out still makes no copy
